description.purpose: The files of one knowledge space, each a logical file hive under one address: `fh-<12 hex>` for the file, `@<hex>` for a version of it. Content lives as content-addressed blocks and immutable versions in the space's one store; every file has one main line that moves only by compare-and-swap on the version a writer read; workspaces are copy-on-write views committed in two phases. No answer names where a file lives -- moving its rows into another space's store changes no address (ADR 0047). Since 1.1.0 ([#905](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/905), [#906](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/906), [#907](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/907), [#908](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/908)) the child hive `./projection` lays a workspace out on a disk, runs a permitted program in it and carries it into git and back, `in_ingest` stores a document a channel sent, and `in_schemas`/`in_tool` put the file tools on a model's menu; lanes joined, so it is the second digit. Since 1.1.1 ([#929](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/929)) the finished document turn leaves `./ingest` for the space without restoring its TTL; the door of the generation it enters restores it. A repair, so it is the third digit. Since 1.2.0 ([#944](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/944)) the head of every file is cut into nodes with semantic anchors and extracted links, answered on the ops `outline`, `links` and `near` and on the tools `file_outline` and `file_links`, and every head that moves leaves the space as `source_changed`; a caller can ask for what it could not before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.3.0 ([#947](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/947), [#918](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/918)) a path is claimed before any op that takes it, so two writers never create one path twice; directories are rows of their own (`create_dir`, `remove_dir`, `dir_info`, `dir_summary`) whose counts follow their files in constant work; `move`, `copy`, `write_node` and `insert` at an anchor change a file by its structure; every summary carries tags; and a described head leaves the space once as `source_described`. Ops, tools and a lane joined, so it is the second digit. Since 1.3.1 ([#973](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/973), [#975](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/975)) the directory derivation is bounded to its hop budget, a directory page may be empty while `next` is set, and a projection job's file steps arrive with the full colony TTL. A promise repaired, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.0 ([#980](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/980), [#994](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/994)) a writer tests, exports and pushes with one call each (`file_ws_exec`, `file_ws_export`, `file_ws_push`, on the menu only where `projection_tools` is "1"), `ws_commit` echoes the workspace name, `git` and `git.<…>` are names reserved for the git projection, a `page` 0 or 1 on a version without pages is ignored (`ignored: ["page"]`) instead of `page_unknown`, `./summarizer` declares `hop.dropped` ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) and the space pins `projection@1.1.0`. A caller can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.4.1 the two `in_derive` edges (`./write` and `./ws` to `./derive`) restore the colony TTL like their `in_dirs` siblings, so a derive job behind a run keeps its budget ([#995](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/995)); no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.2 `file_insert` `after` the line after the last appends at the end as `after` the last line does, and any other line outside the file answers `out_of_range` with the line count and a message naming the ways to append ([#996](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/996)); no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.3 ([#999](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/999)) `./summarizer` declares the optional hop key `unverified`, the sampling fields sent without a `supported_params` list to check them; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.5 ([#801](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/801)) its embedder takes the provider key as a sealed vault grant (`credential_grant_id`, asked on `credential_request`, answered on `in_sealed`) instead of `MEMORY_EMBED_API_KEY` from the process environment; a literal key in the instance still works for 0.62.x while no grant is set. Where a key comes from is a repair of the promise, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.6 ([#1085](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1085)) `read` and `derive` take shares of the reading model's window (`input_soft`, else the catalogue row of the model they are born on, `input_soft_fallback`) instead of fixed character caps: a cut line, hit or diff carries its mark and says how to get the rest, a regex over a line past the budget is refused with the numbers, and `derive` embeds a long section as several pieces. A repair of the promise, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.7 ([#1094](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1094)) `./summarizer` keeps its contract on the `credential_request` route: `finish_reason` is required on every answer but optional on that route, which carries only the grant. Without it a colony that validates emissions dropped the request as `contract_violation`; a contract that admits what the cell already sends is a repair, so it is the third digit. Since 1.4.8 ([#1097](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1097)) the summarizer's, the embedder's and `derive`'s operation timeouts and backstops come from the timeout chain of `docs/cell-types.md`; no lane moved, so it is the third digit.
description.use_when: Wherever text or documents have to be kept, read by line and changed by many writers without losing a change: send a request on `in_read`, `in_write` or `in_ws` of the hive path with `hop.op` and `hop.op_id`, draw `answer` back to the caller.
description.not_in_scope: No disk, `exec` or git in the hive itself -- the child hive `./projection` carries all three; no tool for `raw` or `ws_tree`; no anchors inside a file (`#...` is refused with `anchor_unsupported`); no rights -- who reaches the hive path may read and write.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed). Entry on `hop.route`: in_read, in_write, in_ws, in_model, in_schemas, in_tool. Exit: answer, model_refused, derived, tool_schemas, tool_result.

REQUEST - body `{op, file, args}`, hop `op`, `op_id` (required, mirrored), `ws` (optional workspace name), `mode` (search only), `caller` (internal callers only). Worked: {"op": "read", "file": "/notes/plan.md", "args": {"from": 1, "to": 40}} on `in_read` answers `{ok, op, op_id, file, version, lines, from, to, text}` with every line as `<n>:<h4>|<text>`.
ADDRESS - `fh-<12 hex>` or a path `/a/b.md`, optionally `@<hex prefix>`, `@ws:<name>` or `@snap:<name>`; every answer names the file by its id and the version by its first 12 hex digits.
